newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler workers protest sick pay cuts.
newsitem.headline: Daimler workers protest sick pay cuts.

text.p: Several hundred workers at the Mercedes-Benz AG gearbox plant near Stuttgart put down tools Thursday in protest at Daimler-Benz AG's decision to cut sick pay, the first of several actions planned.
Some 300 workers on the plant's early shift took a break from their work to gather at the factory's front gate to hold a demonstration.
Helmut Lense, the head of the works council at Daimler's plant in Untertuerkheim, said it was a "disgrace" that Daimler has taken a leading role in cutting back sick benefits.
Later this morning, workers at two other Mercedes plants were due to also temporarily stop work.

Daimler on Tuesday stepped to the forefront in implementing controversial legislation passed by German parliament earlier this month that allows companies to pay 80 percent compenstation on sick days, down from the previous 100 percent.
Union and some political leaders say the law only applies to future contracts and companies should not use it to rewrite existing agreements.
Daimler's works council and unions said Wednesday that Daimler's 220,000-strong workforce in Germany would refuse to work overtime and weekend shifts.
